name: Outcome-Only (Raw)
tagline: No reward-space normalization: pass the per-token outcome reward through unchanged and let GRPO downstream do all normalization.
diff_from_baseline: Shao et al., 'DeepSeekMath' / GRPO (arXiv:2402.03300); verl default reward-handling path (`ray_trainer.py` writes raw `token_level_scores`). Naive pass-through baseline — GRPO advantage estimator handles all centering/scaling itself.

name: Group-Std (GRPO upstream)
tagline: Per-prompt-group whitening at the reward stage: subtract group mean, divide by group std (+eps), then re-place at the last response token.
formula: $$s_i = \sum_t r_{i,t},\quad \tilde{s}_i = \frac{s_i - \mu_{g(i)}}{\sigma_{g(i)} + \epsilon},\quad \mu_g, \sigma_g \;\text{computed over samples sharing prompt}\; g$$
diff_from_baseline: Shao et al., 'DeepSeekMath' / GRPO (arXiv:2402.03300); mirrors verl's `compute_grpo_outcome_advantage` but moves it upstream of the advantage estimator. Because GRPO re-normalizes, this baseline tests the effect of double-normalization.

name: Batch-Std Whitening
tagline: Classic RLHF reward whitening: subtract the batch-wide mean and divide by the batch std before placing the scalar back at the last response token.
diff_from_baseline: Stiennon et al., 'Learning to summarize from human feedback' (NeurIPS 2020) and Ouyang et al., 'InstructGPT' (2022) — value-function / reward whitening are the standard RLHF analog. TRL exposes the same as `whiten_rewards`. Common in PPO-RLHF.

name: Length-Aware ($1/\sqrt{T}$)
tagline: DAPO-style length-bias correction: divide each response's scalar reward by $\sqrt{\text{response length}}$ to keep per-sequence gradient contribution length-invariant.
diff_from_baseline: Liu et al., 'DAPO: Decoupled Clip and Dynamic Sampling Policy Optimization' (arXiv:2503.14476, 2025) and 'Dr. GRPO' (arXiv:2503.20783). Counters length bias in GRPO group-mean normalization where verbose responses accumulate more per-token gradient mass.
